hook: The general who won American independence, then gave up power.

pages.x: George Washington was born in Virginia in 1732. His father died when he was 11, and at 16 he worked as a surveyor in the wilderness. The famous story of him chopping down a cherry tree and saying "I cannot tell a lie" was made up by a writer after his death.

In 1754, aged 22, he led Virginia soldiers into the Ohio country and fired some of the first shots of the French and Indian War. The next year he survived a disastrous ambush with four bullet holes in his coat and two horses shot from under him.

In 1775 Congress made him commander of the new American army. On Christmas night 1776, after months of defeats, he led his ragged army across the icy Delaware River and surprised the enemy at Trenton.

In the winter of 1777 his army camped at Valley Forge with too little food, clothing or shoes, and about 2,000 men died of disease. He held the army together, and it came out of the winter trained and tougher.
In 1781, with a French army and fleet, he trapped the British general Cornwallis at Yorktown, in Virginia. The British surrendered, and the war was as good as won.

Instead of making himself king, he resigned his command in 1783 and went home to farm. King George III is said to have called that the act of the greatest man in the world. In 1789 he became the first president, and stepped down after two terms.
By the time he was president he had only one of his own teeth left. His false teeth were not wooden, as legend says, but made of hippopotamus ivory, human teeth and metal springs.
Washington owned enslaved people at Mount Vernon all his life. In his will he ordered that the people he owned be freed after his wife's death. He died in 1799.
Washington led the colonies to independence and set the example of a leader who steps down. He is called the "Father of His Country", and the capital bears his name.
pts: Led the army that won American independence
First president of the United States
Gave up power when he could have kept it
